{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study evaluates structure-activity relationship (SAR) models, which are in silico methods, not whole, live non-human animals. It assesses the predictive capacity of these models against toxicological endpoints, but does not report quantitative agreement between animal model results and human clinical results.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The current study sought to assess and compare the predictions of the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) categories and Dangerous Goods (DG) classifications based on Lethal Dose (LD50) from several available tools",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study assesses toxicological endpoints, which are not specific to a single therapeutic area but are broadly applicable across drug development and chemical safety.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "Several public efforts are aimed at discovering patterns or classifiers in the high-dimensional bioactivity space that predict tissue, organ or whole animal toxicological endpoints. The current study sought to assess and compare the predictions of the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) categories and Dangerous Goods (DG) classifications based on Lethal Dose (LD50) from several available tools (ACD/Labs, Leadscope, T.E.S.T., CATMoS, CaseUltra).",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study evaluates structure-activity relationship models and their predictions for toxicological endpoints, but does not specify or analyze results from any particular animal species.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study assesses predictions of GHS categories and DG classifications based on Lethal Dose (LD50), which are measures of toxicity rather than hard clinical outcomes like mortality or survival."
}
